title: a pipeline run's fixed cost is measured stage by stage and cut by infrastructure
desiredOutcome: the tokens and time a pipeline run spends are attributed to stages and to the files each stage reads, by offline tools with tests, and an infrastructure design that cuts the fixed part is chosen on that evidence with its saving predicted and a benchmark that will confirm or refute it

findings.issue: No case can catch a broken check behind the '(agrees)' verdict. That verdict compares a rebuilt final request's cache read with the prefix identity's prediction, and the analysis (§1.1) cites it as evidence. I mutated a scratch copy and two mutations stayed green at 21/21: `verdict = ("agrees" if True` (M6), and `cr = predicted` in the single-dispatch branch (M7). The fixture's residual and identity always agree, so no case ever produces 'DIFFERS'. A third mutation also stayed green: `one_hour = False` (M8), because every subagent in the fixture writes at the five-minute rate. Today's verdicts are correct: I rebuilt both by hand (29497+513=30010, 22133+1337=23470). The gap is that a regression would print the same evidence word with the suite green. P117.1's outcome says scratch mutations 'each turned their intended case red: sc1-sc21', but it names no command or exit code.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Add a case whose modelUsage cacheRead is off from the identity by a known k, and assert that 'DIFFERS by k' is printed and '(agrees)' is not. Add a case with a one-hour subagent write, and assert the rebuilt request's cw1. Show both red against the two mutations above.

findings.issue: C3 needs the reviewer to write, and the design does not say so. C3 says 'Each agent files its return through a verb … and the agent hands back one line'. Under decision 3(a) that file goes into the committed evidence directory. The reviewer's definition says 'You have Bash so you can LOOK' and 'Must not: anything that writes'. The design still says 'Guarantees. None is weakened' and 'The enforced and followed tables lose no row'. The README row 'the reviewer cannot edit' is still literally true, because Bash is not Edit. But the reviewer's read-only contract has to be loosened for C3 to work: if the main loop filed the reviewer's return instead, the hand-back would land back in its context and the C3 saving would be lost. T3 lists 'both agent prompts' as files to change without saying this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): In C3's Guarantees and in T3, name the loosening: the reviewer gains one write, and say where it goes. Say how it is held, for example a filing verb that can only write the reviewer's own return path, checked by commit-scope. Alternatively, choose 3(b) for the reviewer and state the trade.

findings.issue: The design lists 'the stamp comparison' as one of eight fixed per-task requests, and the stream does not show that. In feature-C-1 the comparison ran inside the gate request (…nt66Ew ran run-test-gate.py and then stamp-verification.py compare in one Bash call). The separate request …yyXaVM was a re-check: its own text reads 'The stamp came back stale, so I'll check which field moved'. The second close attempt was a retry after zsh passed `$V` as one word. The design names that one-off, but only per candidate, not in the §5 headline. The analysis §4 lists six per-task steps (start, dispatch, gate, review dispatch, commit, done), so the two documents disagree. Through m = 4 + 8N, both repeats are assumed to happen on every one of five tasks, and that feeds C7's 0.0795 per task and the 8→5 reduction in §5.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Describe …yyXaVM as a re-check after a stale verdict, with its recurrence unmeasured. Give §1.2 and §5 with m = 4+6N beside 4+8N, or state how much of the 43.0% and 41.1% comes from removing the two repeats. Make the analysis and the design agree on the per-task count.

findings.issue:
Arithmetic problems in the cost model:
(a) The task formula adds c·r·2·(N−1) for the release and the report re-reading earlier tasks. The measured 0.7742 per task already includes those two requests' reads of its task, so this counts them twice (0.0400 at N=5 today, 0.0165 after).
(b) C1 subtracts 9 × 16952 from the executor's 180263 cache reads to get 27695. The executor's first request read 0, so the right figure is 8 × 16952, giving 44647. The read term becomes 0.1264, not 0.1229, and the net per task 0.0593, not 0.0627. The verdict does not change.
(c) Some figures cannot be reproduced from what is shown. C6b's −0.0653 has no arithmetic. C7's 0.0264 'not already in the run class' has none either. The run figure 0.3291 needs an unstated ~0.0109 for reads made before the prose was written, beyond the 'three quantities' the text names.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Drop the 2(N−1) term, or justify it. Correct 27695 to 44647. Write out the arithmetic for −0.0653 and 0.0264, and add the early-reads term to the §5 run line.
fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Pick one quantity, either read-first only or the entry total, and restate every row and target in it. Make `--gate` measure exactly that quantity.

findings.issue: listing() counts every command's description as always-on, including the 8 of 21 commands that set `disable-model-invocation: true`. At HEAD those 8 account for 2860 of the 9659 listing bytes. The design's own §0.1 marks R4, 'descriptions out of startup context', as shipped through exactly that frontmatter. So the analysis prints a measured always-on figure that the design's premise says is about 30% too high. No case covers this rule.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Leave out of the listing any command or skill whose frontmatter sets disable-model-invocation: true. Add a fixture case for it, show it red, and regenerate §6's block.

findings.issue:
Two problems with how manifest edits are classed:
- An Edit of plan state is classed as `file` work. The tool result goes through classify(), which treats a plan-state path as `task`, but the emitted Edit bytes always go to `file` through emitFile. In feature-C-1, plan's $file of 0.0082 is the Edit of docs/audit/audit-plan.json, and the pilot shows the same for 0.0074.
- The plan-state rule for the Read and Edit tools has no case. Mutating line 592 to always return "file" (M14) stays green at 21/21. sc12 covers only the Bash `cat` form.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Class emitted Edit/Write bytes by their target path, the same way classify() does. Add sc12 shapes for Read and Edit of docs/audit/audit-plan.json and show them red against M14.

findings.issue: The confirming benchmark's protocol is cited at docs/research/benchmark-feature-design.md. That file is not on this branch or on main. It exists only at a289dcbb, on the unmerged branch audit/p116-a-whole-feature-in-an-existing. P117 does not declare P116 in blockedBy. The citation is a code span, so the link lint will not catch it, and if P117 lands first its §7 points at nothing.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Declare P117 blockedBy P116, or say in the text that the protocol lands with P116.

findings.issue: Several re-derivation commands use refs that move: `--ref main`, `--ref HEAD`, and `git diff --stat f7eaade4 HEAD`. `main` already resolves to 17570502, not the a73b836a9e8c printed in the analysis. Once T2 changes the reference files, the 'At HEAD' figures can no longer be re-derived with the printed command.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Pin the SHAs the figures were taken at (a73b836a, 7b489337), as the T1 target already does.

findings.issue:
Three claims go beyond their basis:
(a) §8.5 says 'The plugin cannot set it', but C6a and §9 call the same question unknown, and the host facts only say it is not documented.
(b) The design says 'R8's risky arm gates on computed properties instead'. R8 (token-efficiency-audit.md:644-646) gates on task.risk med/high OR redFirst not proved OR the gate disagreeing.
(c) Every dollar prediction uses w = 8.0, the one-hour main-loop write. The host facts say that is the default only on a subscription within plan usage; an API key gets five minutes. §1.4 does not list this.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): In §8.5, call it unknown. Restate R8's `risky` arm accurately. Add the TTL and billing assumption to §1.4.

findings.issue: The analysis says 'The differences have two causes' (output apportioned by input share, and missing final requests) as if measured. No arithmetic splits the published-minus-billed differences between those two causes.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.3-2sz (9501aa91): Mark it as inference, or show the decomposition.

findings.issue: R2 only partly holds. The reviewer's new write is now named, but the claim about what holds it is stronger than the mechanism described. C3 says the verb 'takes the task id and the role, and no path argument … So the only file this write can produce is the reviewer's own return.' That conclusion does not follow. The task id and the role both come from the caller, so a reviewer's one call can write the executor's return for the same task, or a return for any other task. T3's three cases (a path-like argument refused, a malformed return writes nothing, the written path equals the derived one) do not pin either one. This matters because `done --from-return` takes the outcome, `verifiedBy` and `redFirst` from the filed returns (lines 467-469). An executor return that the reviewer overwrote would become the recorded claim, and the claim-to-task binding is what the reviewer exists to check. The fix task asked for 'one filing verb that can only write the reviewer's own return path'. The same overstatement is repeated in the §4 table ('held to its own return by the filing verb'), in §5's *What it does not do*, in §8.3 and in T3 ('Those cases are what holds the write to the reviewer's own return').
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.4-2sz (adece536): Pick one of two. (a) Make the verb write-once for each task and role: it refuses a second filing and leaves the first byte-identical. Add that as a fourth T3 case. Then list under *What nothing checks* that the role and task id are the caller's word, so a filing under a role or task not yet filed is a followed rule. (b) Keep the mechanism and change the claim: replace 'the reviewer's own return' with 'a return path the verb derives from the task id and role it is given', move the caller-chosen role and task id under *What nothing checks*, and reword the four echoes to match.

fixed in P117.4-2sz (adece536): Compute t at k = 6 the way §5 computes the after state: positional reads over the six-request shape, (2616×6 + 5159×5 + 1458×4 + 3646×3 + 1195×2 + 2985×1) × r, against today's 99642 × r. Restate the k = 6 figures above. For C5 and C7, either add the shifted read or say it is left out.

findings.issue: R9's pin for the stream-cost figures still moves. The pin is 'the commit that last changed this document' (`git log -1 -- <doc>`), so it moves with every later edit of the document. The design already plans such an edit: T5 is 'an addendum' to this file, and it lands after T1 changes `tools/stream-cost.py`. From then on, the printed command points at a different tool than the one these figures came from. The other pins (a73b836a, 7b489337, f7eaade4, v3.1.0) are fixed and reproduce.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.4-2sz (adece536): Now that the commit exists, write `9501aa91` in. A later commit can name an earlier one. Alternatively, name the tool's blob (`git rev-parse <commit>:tools/stream-cost.py`), which is known before the commit is made.

findings.issue: This diff did not change these lines. C7's confirming reading and T4's target read 'at most 5 plan, gate and close requests per task' off `per stage, as billed` → `req`. Those stages also hold the five run-level requests. In feature-C-1: plan 5 + gate 3 + close 5 = 13 = 5 run-level + 8 per task. So a one-task after-session would read 10 and fail a target it actually meets. The second clause, `7 + 5N` main-loop requests, is stated correctly.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.4-2sz (adece536): Either subtract the five run-level requests before dividing by N, or keep only the `7 + 5N` clause.

findings.file: docs/research/pipeline-cost-design.md T3, T4, C7; tools/stream-cost.py stage rule
findings.issue: Found by the P117.4 executor; an inference, since no arm C session has run. The confirming after-study is arm C, which plans with /audit:phase add and /audit:task add. The stage rule counts everything from the end of orient to the executor dispatch as plan work. So T4's request clauses and T3's per-task output and token readings would count planning requests, and could refute a change that meets them. The targets were calibrated on an /audit:run session, which plans nothing.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.4-2sz (adece536): T1 adds a stage split that reports requests under a planning command apart from the task cycle's plan work. T3, T4 and C7's confirming reading exclude planning and name the row they read. The assumptions section states that the calibration session planned nothing and that arm C does.

findings.issue: T3 and C3's confirming readings are said to be 'the task cycle with planning excluded' (596, 1100-1101), but sign-off is still counted in them. The after-study is arm C (§7, 1161), and arm C's prompt runs the phase 'with /audit:phase <its id> through sign-off' (<h2>/plugin-sentence.txt). So sign-off's main-loop output lands in `output pool, measured: main loop`, and its task-class tokens land in `contexts:` → `main`, `task`. Neither prediction (4472, 9547) counts them. The new T1 bullet lists the readings that need the sign-off split as 'C7's and T4's "before sign-off", section 7's whole-set reading and T5's S' (1030-1031). T3 is not on that list. §7's T4 row says 'before sign-off'; its T3 row (1172) does not. The margins for one task are small: 5000 − 4472 = 528 tokens and 11000 − 9547 = 1453. Sign-off spawns a reviewer (§1.4, 244), and C3 computes no brief for it. In `feature-C-1` the per-task reviewer brief was 2817 output tokens. A sign-off brief that size would put a one-task session over the output target. That is the same class as R15 and R16: a target refuted by work the prediction never counted. Because sign-off is paid once per session, the flip is likely at small N rather than at every N. But §7 confirms a target only when every after session meets it, so a single small-N session is enough to break it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.5-2sz (fd0d366d): Add 'before sign-off' to both C3 readings (600-607), to both T3 output bullets (1103-1107) and to §7's T3 row. Add T3 and C3 to T1's list of readings that need the sign-off split (1030-1031), under the same rule as the others: a reading that cannot place sign-off says so.

findings.issue: Two gaps in T1's planning rule. (a) The span closes only at another command or at `audit-task.py start`. The `add` invocation has already loaded the whole of phase.md, including its run section (`git show 7b489337:plugins/audit/commands/phase.md`, line 37). If the model then runs the phase without a new Skill call, every request between the last `add` and the first `start` reads as planning. Those are section 1.2's run-level preflight, manifest read and lock (in feature-C-1, main-loop requests 2-4 come before the start at 5). That contradicts 'So `plan` keeps the run's own requests' (1024-1025). T4's 'less the run's own five' then subtracts requests that are no longer in plan, gate or close, which biases the reading toward a pass. (b) T1's only planning target is the empty row on `feature-C-1` (1041-1042). An implementation that never reports planning also passes it.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.5-2sz (fd0d366d): (a) Also close the span at the first main-loop request that runs a plugin script other than the `audit-task.py add`/`add-phase` verbs (the preflight or the lock). Or state the case and have T4 subtract only the run-level requests that fall outside planning. (b) Add a positive target: `whole-C-2`'s stream, whose main-loop Skill call `{"skill": "audit:phase", "args": "add"}` must open a non-empty `planning` row. Add a twin fixture in which `start` closes the span.

findings.issue: The whole-set reading subtracts the `planning` row's `$total`. That total holds every prose write made inside the span. By the design's own T2 table (1064), `/audit:phase add` reads 242068 bytes first at `7b489337`: phase.md lines 9-12 name all four reference files before any verb is chosen. After T2, `add` may still read up to 30000 bytes. Prose that a planning command reads and the run then reuses would come out of the session total, while §5's run class predicts it. The reading would then come in under the prediction for a reason the change did not cause.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.5-2sz (fd0d366d): Subtract only planning's own task-class part (its `out` and the `task` tokens T1 prints for it). Or subtract the planning row less its `Read <plugin>/reference/…` writes. Or state the prose case beside the row.

findings.issue: Two constants are left in T4's readings. (a) §7's T4 row reads '`req` per task, before sign-off, with the `planning` row apart'. It omits 'less the run's own five', which T4 (1119-1120) and C7 (812-817) now require. Read off the table, `feature-C-1` gives 13 per task, not 8. (b) The second clause fixes orient at 2 ('which adds orient's 2'). Orient ends at the first call that is not a plugin read (`tools/stream-cost.py:337-338`). A Skill call is not a plugin read, so an arm C session whose first request makes the `add` call has an orient of 0. `7 + 5N` would then sit 2 above what that session can reach, which also biases toward a pass.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.5-2sz (fd0d366d): (a) Add 'less the run's own five (section 1.2)' to §7's T4 row. (b) In T4's second clause, read orient's request count off the session's `per stage, as billed` instead of fixing it at 2.

findings.issue: The write-once guarantee and the four echoes (887, 996-998, 1096-1099, 1223-1225) are accurate. Two premises around them are stated as facts, with no mechanism and no T3 case. (a) 'The reviewer is dispatched only once the executor's return is filed, because its brief carries that return as filed.' Handing the brief over is itself a followed rule (540-541), and nothing says `brief` refuses to compose a reviewer brief before the executor's return is filed. (b) 'its own task is left with none, and `done --from-return` refuses that close (above).' The 'above' (542) says only that it refuses 'when no return is filed'. No case pins a close with one role's return missing, or which start's returns the close reads.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.5-2sz (fd0d366d): Either specify both and pin each with a T3 case: `brief` for the reviewer exits non-zero until the executor's return for the current start is filed, and `done --from-return` refuses unless both roles' returns for the current start are filed. Or move both sentences under *What nothing checks* as followed rules.

findings.issue: Found by the P117.5 executor. stream-cost.py keeps only the last result event of a stream. A headless session that is re-invoked, for example when a background task notifies it, emits several result events, each carrying the usage of its own stretch. whole-C-3 has three, and their usage blocks sum exactly to its main loop. Read with only the last one, the main loop prints DISAGREE, Opus prices differ by about half a dollar, and an orphan request is printed with negative tokens. So the tool cannot price a whole-feature arm C session, and T5's calibration on those sessions is blocked.
findings.resolution: fixed in P117.6-2sz (9e4ab790): Read every result event: sum their usage and modelUsage per model, and keep each final request's rebuild per result segment. Add a case with a stream holding two result events whose sum is known, plus a twin with one, and show it red against keeping only the last. Re-run the tool on all whole-C sessions and on the four recorded sessions; the latter's figures must not move.

findings.issue: The per-task ratio favours the plugin, and the document never says so. The top of the ratio is the task cycle, which leaves out the plugin's session-level work: the session-start write is in planning, and the report is in the run's close. The bottom is arm A's whole session, which keeps plain's session-level work. Measured with the result-reading commit's `analyse()` costs, arm A's first request (session-start write plus the file listing) and its last (the closing summary) cost 0.0793, 0.0955 and 0.0877. That is 15.7, 15.9 and 16.4 percent of whole-A-1, -2 and -3. With those two requests taken out of the bottom (mean 0.459507 instead of 0.547004), the predicted ratios change. Rung 1 becomes 2.05 / 1.95 / 2.18, mean 2.06, not 1.72 / 1.64 / 1.83. G2 becomes 1.60 / 1.50 / 1.75. G1 becomes 1.40 / 1.29 / 1.55, mean 1.41, not 1.17 / 1.09 / 1.30, mean 1.19. Section 5.1's single-task shape compares a whole plugin session with a whole plain session, so it treats both sides alike. It gives 2.16 at rung 1, which agrees with the fairer reading. The document's 0.2 says only that 'the description leaves the plain side open'. The gap matters because it is larger than both margins the headlines rest on. Rung 1's 'meets the ceiling in every session' and G1's 'meets the ideal on the arm's mean' both reverse under the fairer reading, and the user chose G1 partly on the second.
findings.resolution: Next to the definition in 0.2, say that the bottom holds plain's session-level open and close and the top does not, and give the size. Print the per-task ratio both ways in 5.1's ladder: against whole arm A, and against arm A less its first and last main-loop requests (or add the plugin's equivalent session-start write to the cycle). Restate the rung 1 and G1 claims in 5.2 and section 8 for each reading, and say which one the target means. Put that same quantity in section 7's per-task row, so the after-study measures what the decision used.

findings.issue: G1's guarantee change is stated as 'the per-task intent check moves', but G1 removes more than that, and the way it is held may never fire. (a) The per-task review returns two more answers. One is a red-first grade: a `not-proved` on a `tdd` task becomes a human action item (execute-task.md:352). The other is the inherited-test question. That question is bounded by `tests.gate`, which only a task-mode review receives. Under G1 the phase review is not handed any task's `tests.gate`, so the inherited-test question comes back `not-asked` by construction, and phase mode grades red-first as `not-attempted`. Neither is listed as given up or moved. (In these sessions neither caught anything: all nine per-task reviews returned `inheritedTests: not-asked`, and their red-first words echoed the executor's: `proved` six times, `could-not-prove` three times. So the decision may well stand, but the statement is not exact.) (b) Under 'held by', the phase brief carries each task's return and description but not its commit or diff. The reviewer definition's stated reason for asking per task is exactly that the phase diff 'has no way back to the task that produced each line'. (c) With no per-task reviewer filing a return, T3's `done --from-return` forces every G1 task to close `--intent not-asked` with a basis. T6's sign-off refusal accepts 'a `not-asked` with its basis', and today's sign-off already counts a deliberate `not-asked` as answered (execute-task.md:373-377). Read literally, every G1 task meets the refusal at its own close, so the refusal never fires. T6's micro-test would only catch this if its fixture closes tasks the G1 way, and T6 does not say it does.
findings.resolution: In C14, the section 4 table, 5.2 and section 8 decision 1, name everything G1 removes per task: the intent binding before commit, the red-first grade, and the inherited-test question. Then either carry each into the phase review or list it as given up. Have the phase reviewer's computed brief (T3/T6) carry each task's commit SHA and its `tests.gate` commands, and ask the binding, red-first and inherited-test questions per task. Give a G1 task a close state that is not `not-asked`, such as one recording that its intent is deferred to the phase review, and make the sign-off verb refuse unless the phase review answered for that task. Pin it with a T6 case: a fixture whose tasks closed the G1 way must be refused at sign-off when one binding is missing.

findings.issue: Section 5.3 says 'Any one of them can double and the worst session stays under the ceiling'. Two rows do not support that. (a) The requests row uses C7's 5 per task instead of 4, a 25 percent rise. Doubling it to 8 per task adds 12 × (37755 × 0.2e-6 + 250 × 20e-6) = 0.1506, which puts whole-C-2-r at 2.10. (b) Output and writes are treated as independent, but the main loop's output is written back into its own cache at the next request. In whole-A-1, 10016 of 12166 output tokens came back as main-loop cache writes (0.82, from the tool's `items`). Rung 1 sets W = 3000 below O = 3500. Doubling output together with its write-back (about 2870 × 9.3e-6 ≈ 0.027 on top of 0.0700) puts whole-C-2-r at about 2.00. There is also no sensitivity check for G1, the chosen rung. Its mean margin to 1.25 is about 0.035 per session, less than doubling output alone (0.04 before write-back). T11's probe threshold of 500 output tokens per request is taken from this table.
findings.resolution: Double every row, or rename the column to say what each row actually varies. Tie W to O (W ≥ 0.82 × O plus the tool results). Add a G1 table against the 1.25 ideal. Set the probe's output threshold from the tied model.

findings.issue: T1's target says 'the `unattributed` row is gone' on all three arm C records. The stated mechanism, which skips the rebuild for a dispatch whose tool result is the async-launch notice, does not get there on whole-C-2-r. Its two async dispatches are RKf8vq (cacheR 33634) and MMJ2sv (32179), 65813 together, against a row of −70856. That leaves −5043 (dispatch command, and the `dispatch` lines at 9e4ab790). The document itself says that row 'is not yet explained'.
findings.resolution: Limit the target to whole-C-3 and whole-C-1 and keep whole-C-2-r as an open reading. Or add an investigation step to T1 that names the second cause before the target is set.

findings.issue: Several estimates carry the 'estimate' label but no stated judgement, which section 0's label definition requires. In sign-off: each request reads P′ + 4000, writes 600, the final report emits 1000, and the filing request costs 0.005. In G1: 1500 tokens per return in the phase review. They are small. The sign-off ones are about 0.06 of the predicted 0.25–0.27, against a budget margin of 0.07–0.12.
findings.resolution: Base each one on a reading, for example whole-C-3's sign-off requests 45–57 with the span and billed-span commands, or the filed-return size implied by feature-C-1's hand-backs (6142 and 3550 bytes). Or add them to a sensitivity row for the phase-overhead budget.

review.outcome: [findings: 27 - 0 high, 8 med, 19 low; 22 with a recorded fix commit]

tasks.title: a pipeline run's tokens and time are attributed to stages and files by offline tools with tests
tasks.description:
Measures where a pipeline run spends its tokens and time, with offline tools that have tests and make no paid call. Requested by the user on 2026-10-07 after the feature benchmark showed that the plugin pipeline costs several times more than plain Claude Code on a task both solve.

1. Static context measure. A tool computes what each command and agent loads before it does any work: the command file, every reference file the command instructs the model to read, the agent definition, auto-loaded skills, and the always-on cost (plugin listing, CLAUDE.md). It reports bytes and an estimated token count, labelled as an estimate with its rule. It is computed for the pipeline's real path (/audit:run, /audit:next, /audit:phase, sign-off, executor, reviewer), at the published tag and at local main.

2. Stream attribution. A tool reads a recorded stream-json session and attributes every model request's tokens to a stage: the main loop before any dispatch, plan and manifest work, executor, reviewer, gate, close. It splits each stage into cache write, cache read, input and output, priced with the shipped table. It names the file reads that created the largest cache writes. Run it on the recorded plugin sessions: the pipeline pilot, and the plugin arm of the feature benchmark under the internal analysis directory's experiments. Report what each stage cost in each.

3. Tests. Each tool has a selftest that meets the repository's contract, with fixtures. Attribution is proved on a hand-built stream whose answer is known, including a twin that must not move a token between stages.

4. docs/research/pipeline-cost-analysis.md states, from these measurements:
- which part of a run's cost is fixed per run, per task, and per file the work touches;
- what the prompt cache already saves and what it cannot;
- the largest single contributors.
Every figure sits beside the command that re-derives it.

outcome.technical:
Fixes P117-R22. tools/stream-cost.py keeps every result event and tags each request with its stretch.

What the CLI writes in each result event, measured on whole-C-1, whole-C-3 and whole-C-2-r (3, 3 and 5 results):
- usage is per stretch: the main-loop requests between one init and the next sum exactly to that stretch's usage;
